passage: My name is Jomon, and I was in the treasure hunt team. Jeevan said, "We start at the big tree, follow me!" and everyone ran after him. Gauri whispered, "I think the clue means the water tap, not the tree." I heard her, but Jeevan was already far ahead and I did not want to stop the game or make him angry. So I ran to the tree too. We dug around the roots for a long time. The other team found the box at the tap. Gauri did not say "I told you." She just looked at her shoes, and I felt bad.

qa.q: Where did Gauri think the clue pointed?
qa.a: Gauri thought the clue meant the water tap, not the tree.

qa.q: Why did Jomon run to the tree after hearing Gauri?
qa.a: Jomon did not want to stop the game or make Jeevan angry, so keeping the fun and the friendship felt more important than checking; later Jomon felt bad.

qa.q: What could Jomon have done at the moment Gauri whispered?
qa.a: Jomon could have called out "Wait, Gauri has an idea" and asked the team to check both places before digging.

qa.q: How might Gauri feel after the other team found the box at the tap?
qa.a: Gauri may feel disappointed and unheard; looking at her shoes and not saying "I told you" suggests hurt but no wish to blame anyone.

grounding: Children follow the confident child's plan even when a quieter child has a better idea, since arguing seems to risk the fun and the friendship.

passage: Teacher's note, Class 5 relay practice. Uma, always sure of herself, announced the running order and the team fell in line. Tara, the quietest, said softly that Kabir should run last as he was faster at the finish. Nobody replied, and Uma had already moved on. The team came third. Afterwards nobody would say why. Next time I asked each child to name one idea before the order was decided, and told the group that a good plan can come from anyone. Tara nodded and looked surprised to be asked. — Jagdish Sir

qa.q: Who suggested that Kabir should run last?
qa.a: Tara suggested that Kabir should run last.

qa.q: Why did nobody reply when Tara spoke softly about the running order?
qa.a: The team was following Uma's confident lead and nobody wanted to interrupt the plan or risk the fun and the friendship, so Tara's idea slipped past unnoticed.

qa.q: What did Jagdish Sir change that gave a quiet child a chance?
qa.a: Jagdish Sir asked each child to name one idea before the order was decided and said a good plan can come from anyone.

qa.q: How might Tara have experienced being unheard, and then being asked?
qa.a: Tara probably felt overlooked the first time, and the surprised nod when asked suggests being invited to speak was new and welcome.

grounding: Children follow the confident child's plan even when a quieter child has a better idea, and nobody checks for fear of spoiling the game.

passage:
The power had gone out in the whole building, so the children played treasure hunt on the staircase with two torches and ten minutes before Mummy's call for dinner.
Indu took charge at once. “We check the terrace first! Hemant, come!”
Little Babloo, who never talked much, tugged Hemant's sleeve. “The clue said ‘where shoes sleep’. Isn't that the shoe rack on the ground floor?”
Hemant thought Babloo was right. But Indu was already racing up, shouting, “Terrace team, go go go!” Everyone was laughing. If he stopped, the fun would stop.
So Hemant ran up too. They searched the terrace in the dark and found nothing. Then Mummy called. On the way down, Hemant shone his torch on the shoe rack. The paper was there.

qa.q: What did the clue say?
qa.a: The clue said "where shoes sleep".

qa.q: Why did Hemant run up to the terrace despite agreeing with Babloo?
qa.a: He was worried that stopping to argue would spoil the fun, and he felt carried along by Indu's excitement.

qa.q: What could Hemant try next time the group rushes off?
qa.a: He could quickly say, "Wait, Babloo has an idea," or suggest splitting up, so the quieter child's idea gets checked without ending the game.

qa.q: How might Babloo feel when the paper turned up on the shoe rack?
qa.a: Babloo may feel quietly proud to be right but also disappointed and unheard, since nobody listened.

grounding: Shows children following a confident child's plan in a group game while a quieter child's better idea is ignored, to keep the fun going.

passage:
Sunday cricket in the colony lane: B-block against C-block. Avni, the tallest, decided everything. “I'll open. Zubin, you bowl first.”
Kunal, from the third floor, said softly, “Their best batsman can't play spin. Maybe Farzana should bowl first? She bowls spin.”
Avni didn't hear, or pretended not to. “Zubin, fast balls. Let's go!”
Zubin looked at Kunal. Kunal was probably right. But Avni was already clapping and everyone was cheering. Arguing would make it feel like a fight.
Zubin bowled fast. C-block's batsman hit him for three fours. Farzana finally bowled in the fourth over and got him out first ball. Avni said, “Great!” as if it had been her idea.

qa.q: Who got C-block's batsman out?
qa.a: Farzana got him out first ball.

qa.q: What was Zubin feeling when he looked at Kunal?
qa.a: Zubin felt doubtful and a bit uneasy, thinking Kunal was right but not wanting a fight to spoil the game.

qa.q: What went wrong in the team's plan, and what would help?
qa.a: Nobody checked Kunal's idea because arguing felt risky; letting everyone say one idea before the match would help.

qa.q: How might Kunal see the moment Avni said "Great!"?
qa.a: Kunal might feel overlooked and a bit frustrated, since the plan worked but nobody gave Kunal credit.

grounding: Shows children following a confident child's plan in a lane game though a quieter child's idea was better, because arguing risks the fun.

passage:
“Blanket fort! Everyone, pillows on the floor!” Nazia shouted.
“But the blanket keeps falling,” said little Pinky. “Can we use the dining chairs? Like poles?”
“No, no, my way,” Nazia said. “Pillows stacked high. Yamini, get more pillows.”
Yamini looked at Pinky's chair idea. It made sense. “Um, maybe—”
“Yamini! Pillows!”
Yamini fetched the pillows. They stacked them. The blanket fell on their heads twice. Everyone giggled the first time, not the second.
Pinky whispered, “Chairs would work.”
“Shh,” Yamini whispered back. “Nazia will get upset.”
When Ammi walked in, she moved two chairs over without a word. The fort stood up at once.

qa.q: What did Pinky suggest using?
qa.a: She suggested using the dining chairs, like poles.

qa.q: Why did Yamini say "Shh" to Pinky?
qa.a: Yamini felt worried that Nazia would get upset and the fun would end, so Yamini kept quiet despite thinking chairs made sense.

qa.q: How could a parent support the children next time?
qa.a: A parent could suggest that everyone shares one idea before building, so Pinky's plan gets a turn without anyone feeling bossed.

qa.q: What is it like for Pinky when the idea keeps being brushed aside?
qa.a: Pinky probably feels small and ignored, especially when Ammi does exactly what Pinky suggested.

grounding: Shows children following the confident child's plan for a fort while a younger child's better idea is ignored to keep peace.

passage:
My name is Ujjwal, and last Sunday we played treasure hunt in our building compound.
Shalini always makes the plans. She said, "All of us search the garden together!" Little Dev said very softly, "We could split up. Two in the garden, two by the parking." Nobody answered him.
I thought Dev was right. But Shalini looked so sure, and I didn't want her to get cross and stop playing. So we all went to the garden.
The other team split up and found all five clues first. Walking home, Dev kicked a stone and didn't talk.
I wish I had said, "Dev's idea is good." Next time I will, even if Shalini frowns.

qa.q: Where did Dev suggest two of them should search?
qa.a: Two by the parking, and two in the garden.

qa.q: Why did Ujjwal stay quiet even though Ujjwal thought Dev was right?
qa.a: Ujjwal was worried Shalini would get cross and stop playing, so keeping the fun and the friendship felt safer than speaking up.

qa.q: What could the group try next time before choosing a plan?
qa.a: They could let everyone share one idea and pick together, so a quiet voice like Dev's gets heard.

qa.q: What was the game like for Dev?
qa.a: Dev likely felt ignored and disappointed, since nobody answered and the idea would have worked; kicking a stone in silence shows it.

grounding: Shows children following the confident child's plan in a group game while a quieter child's better idea goes unheard, because arguing seems to risk the fun.
